descriptor: Regulated wholesale fibre network operator (post-UFB build) · FY ends 30 June · reported in NZD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Chorus Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Chorus Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Chorus Limited: EBITDA is also the anchor for the Commerce Commission's building-blocks/RAB regime and for Chorus' own leverage covenant (net debt/EBITDA, ~4.75x at FY2026, near the top of the company's own policy range). Read it beside CapEx: EBITDA of $726m (FY2026, +3% YoY) is being earned on a network whose build-era capex has stepped down from ~$650-670m p.a. to $375m, which is what is now inflecting free cash flow from structurally negative to positive.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend as the mostly-fixed-cost network absorbs more connections
  • Net debt/EBITDA against Chorus' own leverage tolerance and the 2027 Fibre IM Review's allowed-WACC outcome for PQ3

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Chorus Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Chorus Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Chorus Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Chorus Limited: the UFB fibre build is complete, so gross capex has stepped down from build-era peaks (~$650-670m p.a.) to a sustaining-plus-growth base of $375m in FY2026 (management splits this as ~$205m sustaining, ~$170m growth, though that split isn't in the time series here), guided $375-415m for FY2027. This taper is the main driver of Chorus' free-cash-flow inflection.

What to watch:

  • Gross capex continuing to taper toward the sustaining-only run rate as the copper network is fully retired (target end-CY2028)
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA (working capital, interest paid)

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Chorus Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Chorus Limited: almost all of it is regulated wholesale access revenue billed to ~90 retail service providers (Spark, One NZ, 2degrees and others), not to end consumers. Growth now comes from fibre uptake (75.9% of the UFB footprint at FY2026 year-end, up from ~72% FY2025) and ARPU mix-shift as customers move to faster plans -- not from network expansion, since the UFB build is complete and legacy copper is being retired by 2028.

What to watch:

  • Fibre uptake grinding higher: the remaining growth is the harder-to-win rural/UFB2 cohort (67.5% uptake) against FWA and Starlink competition
  • ARPU trend as the base migrates off copper onto higher-speed fibre plans
  • Interim rows show H1/H2 seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Chorus Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue growth (fibre uptake + ARPU mix-shift)
